about.title: About Me
about.subtitle: Software Engineer
about.description: I am a software engineer who graduated from Atatürk University's Software Engineering program in 2026. During my internship, I designed and deployed a KVKK-compliant, self-hosted enterprise AI support platform (AsistTR) for Atatürk University from scratch; the system will be actively used across the university's network of ~60,000 students.
about.description.original: I graduated from Atatürk University Software Engineering in 2026. I focus on AI/RAG, backend, full-stack and real-time systems, with attention to data, infrastructure, security and operations as well as user-facing product development.
about.atugem: I have hands-on project experience in advanced RAG architectures (RAPTOR, HippoRAG2, Agentic RAG, Self-Reflective RAG, Speculative RAG), full-stack development, and embedded systems (NVIDIA Jetson, Pixhawk PX4).
about.atugem.original: In AsistTR, I combined PostgreSQL/pgvector hybrid retrieval, RRF, query decomposition, HyDE, sufficiency gating, adaptive reranking, evidence/claim validation, semantic cache and Agentic RAG with Node.js, Redis, Socket.IO, BullMQ and WebRTC in one product architecture.
about.bap: I have proven my academic and practical productivity with 1st place at an EU-funded hackathon and TÜBİTAK 2209-A and LKAB-B research support.
about.bap.original: I developed flight software and ground-station systems for TÜRKSAT Model Satellite projects. I also won first place in an EU-funded hackathon with the RAG-powered KamuFlow AI project, and the AXOLOTL research project received TÜBİTAK 2209-A support.
about.cv.new: After my internship, I continued developing AsistTR independently, bringing live support, SLA-based ticketing, CRM/Customer 360, customer portal, workflow automation, AI Agent Studio, WebRTC and omnichannel communications into one platform. The current version is available as a public demo.

projects.sigma2026.title: TÜRKSAT 2026 Model Satellite — NONGRAVITY SIGMA
projects.sigma2026.description: An end-to-end model satellite software system I developed for the SIGMA mission of the TÜRKSAT 2026 Model Satellite Competition. It combines Raspberry Pi 5 flight control, dual-motor active descent and station keeping, encrypted XBee telemetry, Walksnail Avatar video, APAM, ARAS, and an Electron ground station in one architecture.
projects.sigma2026.technologies: Core Technologies: Raspberry Pi 5, Python 3.11, React 19, TypeScript, Electron 43, XBee 3, Arduino C++, Walksnail Avatar, H.264/MJPEG, and WebSocket.
projects.sigma2026.status: Active development · flight and safety scenarios verified with automated tests
projects.sigma2026.summary_text: NONGRAVITY SIGMA is an end-to-end model satellite software system I developed for the TÜRKSAT Model Satellite Competition 2026 SIGMA category. It runs a 10 Hz sensor loop and closed-loop dual ESC control on Raspberry Pi 5, managing autonomous separation, 8–10 m/s active descent, a 10-second position-hold phase at 200 meters and the APAM safety descent sequence.
projects.sigma2026.ownership: All model satellite software—including flight software, the Electron ground station, RF communication protocols, and test infrastructure—was developed from scratch by Nurullah Şahin.
projects.sigma2026.feature_flight: Real-time mission state machine, dual barometers, and closed-loop dual-motor control on Raspberry Pi 5.
projects.sigma2026.feature_rf: Official 1 Hz, 17-field telemetry; production EE=1 encrypted XBee unicast network and Bonus IoT station.
projects.sigma2026.feature_video: Walksnail Avatar primary video, Pi 720p15 local H.264 recording, and XBee 320×180 hot video backup.
projects.sigma2026.feature_safety: SIGMA active descent, 200-meter station keeping, APAM safety sequence, and ARAS fault monitoring.
projects.sigma2026.feature_ground: React, TypeScript, and Electron ground station with telemetry, mission profile, GPS, attitude, video, and voice mission assistant.
projects.sigma2026.validation_text: I verified flight and safety scenarios with automated tests and built an Electron-based ground station that combines telemetry, mission profile, 3D attitude, GPS, ARAS, video and operator commands on one screen. Physical field acceptance remains separate from software validation.

projects.nonGravitySatellite.title: TÜRKSAT 2025 Model Satellite — NONGRAVITY
projects.satellite.description_detailed: End-to-end model satellite software system I developed as software leader for TÜRKSAT Model Satellite Competition 2025. Built from scratch with fully automatic telemetry (1 Hz), real-time video streaming (240x180@2fps), high-quality SD card video recording (640x480@15fps), IoT S2S bonus mission, and SAHA protocol for carrier-payload communication.
projects.nonGravitySatellite.summary_tex: Fully automatic payload system developed by NONGRAVITY Team (286570) for TÜRKSAT Model Satellite Competition 2025. After separation at 400m from rocket-launched model satellite, it descends with its own parachute while transmitting continuous telemetry (1 Hz, 30 fields), real-time video via XBee, and H.264/MP4 recording to SD. Descent speeds: Carrier 12-14 m/s, Payload 6-8 m/s. IoT S2S bonus mission continuously receives temperature data throughout the flight from 2 ground stations at 412-707m distance. Includes SAHA protocol for carrier-payload communication and ARAS alarm system. All software components (Python, C#, Arduino) built from scratch.
projects.nonGravitySatellite.architectur: Carrier Module: Based on Arduino Nano. It undertakes the tasks of collecting sensor data, controlling the separation mechanism, and transmitting basic telemetry data.
Payload Module: Based on Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W. It performs the tasks of transferring camera images, transmitting location information, and controlling the multi-spectral filtering system.
Ground Station: A C#-based desktop application. It provides functions for visualizing telemetry data, sending commands, monitoring and recording camera images.
projects.nonGravitySatellite.hardware_pr: Processors: Raspberry Pi Zero 2W (Payload), Arduino Nano (Carrier), Arduino Nano + Mega 2560 (IoT Stations)
projects.nonGravitySatellite.hardware_se: Sensors: BMP280 Pressure (I2C 0x76/0x77), 10-DOF IMU (ADXL345, ITG3200, HMC5883L), UbloxNeo-8M GPS (UART), ADS1115 16-bit ADC (Battery monitor), DS3231 RTC
projects.nonGravitySatellite.hardware_co: Communication: XBee 3 Pro Module (63mW, 250 Kbps), API Mode 1, PAN ID 0x6570, Mesh Network (Channel 12, 13, 14)
projects.nonGravitySatellite.hardware_ca: Camera: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 (11.9MP) - Dual System: SD Recording (640x480@15fps H.264) + XBee Stream (240x180@2fps MJPEG)
projects.nonGravitySatellite.hardware_po: Power: NCR18650B Li-Ion 3400mAh x2 (Payload), Beston 9V USB-C (Carrier), LM2596 Step-Down + LM2577 Step-Up Regulators
projects.nonGravitySatellite.hardware_me: Actuators: 2x SG90 Servo (Multi-spectral filter + Separation), Passive Buzzer (Recovery signal)
projects.nonGravitySatellite.software_gr: Ground Station: C# Windows Forms (.NET Framework) - Real-time telemetry charts, 3D satellite visualization (OpenGL), map (GMap.NET), live video, ARAS alarm system, CSV export.
projects.nonGravitySatellite.software_ca: Carrier System: Arduino Nano (C++) - BMP280 pressure, automatic separation @400m, SAHA protocol (XBee), buzzer recovery.
projects.nonGravitySatellite.software_pa: Payload: Python 3.11 (Raspberry Pi) - Multi-threaded architecture, 1 Hz telemetry, dual video system, sensor fusion, SD recording, XBee communication, IoT data reception, systemd service.
projects.nonGravitySatellite.software_io: IoT Stations: Arduino Nano + Mega 2560 (C++) - BMP280 temperature, XBee 3 Pro (Channel 12/13), 412-707m distance communication.

projects.sualti.title: Autonomous Underwater Vehicle - AXOLOTL
projects.sualti.description: In the TÜBİTAK 2209-A-supported research project "Configuration and Development of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles," I worked on GPU-accelerated real-time object detection on NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX/Orin Nano and contributed to a Pixhawk PX4-based autonomous control architecture.
projects.axolotl.summary_text: I worked as a project researcher on the study titled "Configuration and Development of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles"; the project received support under the TÜBİTAK 2209-A University Students Research Projects Support Program.
projects.axolotl.feature_design: Original and domestic design: All technical drawings, designs, engineering analyses, and software were developed by team members.
projects.axolotl.feature_hardware: Advanced Hardware: Jetson Xavier NX (artificial intelligence and image processing), Pixhawk PX4 (task management and motor control).
projects.axolotl.feature_sensors: Sensors: Depth, pressure, IMU/compass, ultrasonic sensors, water leak sensors.
projects.axolotl.feature_mechanical: Mechanical Design: Hydrodynamic design in Axolotl form, PETG material, modular and sealed body.
projects.axolotl.feature_software: Software: Python-based image processing (OpenCV, NumPy), task execution, and motor control algorithms.
projects.axolotl.feature_safety: Safety: Water leak sensors, emergency surfacing system, power cut-off system.
projects.axolotl.updates_text: The project aims to improve performance with significant hardware updates such as transitioning from Jetson Nano to Jetson Xavier NX and using the Arducam MINI M12 camera system instead of Lidar. Sealing and hydrodynamic efficiency are prioritized in the mechanical design.

projects.asisttr.summary_text: AsistTR is a self-hosted, multi-tenant and omnichannel support platform I developed for organizations to manage visitor, student, customer and support requests on their own infrastructure. I continued the project independently after my internship and published a public demo.

projects.asisttr.feature3: Socket.IO + Redis Adapter, BullMQ, transactional outbox, PostgreSQL RLS, WebRTC/TURN and a Shadow DOM widget.
projects.asisttr.feature4: Adapter architectures for WhatsApp Cloud API, Telegram, Instagram/Facebook, Twilio SMS/MMS, email and signed webhooks.
